name: East Gurage dialect cluster
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 7 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Hetzron, Robert. 1996. Notes on East Gurage. In Petr Zemánek (ed.), Studies in Near Eastern Languages and Literatures: Memorial Volume of Karel Petráček, 245-259. Prague: Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic, Oriental Institute.
catalog_locator: sec. 2 'Phonology', p. 248, last paragraph before '3. Morphology'; informants and 'no claim is made about dialectal division' p. 245
catalog_quote: Stress is conditioned by the syllabic structure: it falls on the last vowel of the word that is followed by a consonant. In other words, final closed syllables are stressed, and if the final syllable is open, the stress is penultimate. It seems, however, that sentence stress plays a more important role than word stress.

It seems, however, that sentence stress plays a more important role than word stress.' -- verbatim as quoted (the djvu scanned copy, ~line 13418, has trivial scanned slips 'Stress 1s.. 1t falls' but the PD…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Right-edge, closure-sensitive: stress the final syllable if it is closed (ends in a consonant); otherwise stress the penultimate. Word stress is weak relative to sentence stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None; author adds that sentence stress seems to play a more important role than word stress. Context (p. 247-248): vowel length judged non-phonemic 'in the dialects investigated by me'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule stated for the East Gurage dialect cluster as a whole from Hetzron's 1965-66 field data (one Selti, one Wolane [Mr. Nägash Muzäyyän], one 'Enneqor' informant; 'no claim is made about dialectal division', p. 245). Caveat: the modern Wolane grammar (Meyer 2006) has no stress section; its incidental acute-marked examples (p. 38: qetéle, wodérō, wozéne, and yizówrān / yirówṭān with a closed final syllable) all carry the mark on the penult, which may not match Hetzron's 'final closed syllable stressed' clause - seen only in Google Books snippets, not verified in the printed book.
new_statements.identity_note: Hetzron 1996 describes the East Gurage dialect cluster jointly (Selti = Silt'e silt1240, Wolane wola1253, and an 'Enneqor' [Inneqor] variety), one informant each, explicitly making 'no claim about dialectal division'; the stress sentence is not tagged to a single variety. The Wolane-specific reference grammar (Meyer 2006, wola1253 proper) has no stress section (snippet-level check only).

sources.note: Sec. 2 Phonology, p. 248: stress is conditioned by syllable structure - it falls on the last vowel followed by a consonant, i.e. a final closed syllable is stressed, otherwise the penult; sentence stress seems more important than word stress. Data from one Selti, one Wolane and one 'Enneqor' informant (1965-66), stated for the East Gurage cluster without dialect differentiation (p. 245).
